# greet

Compose a single greeting line. Nothing else.

## Steps

1. Read the recipient name from the arguments.
2. No name is available -> say so and stop. Do not invent one.
3. Compose one line: a salutation, the recipient name, and the occasion when given.
4. Show the line and stop.

## Output

One line of plain text. No surrounding commentary, no alternatives list.

files.skills/release-train/SKILL.md:
---
name: release-train
description: Promote the unreleased changelog section to a numbered release across every distribution manifest. Use when the user says "cut a release", "release train", or "bump the version".
---

# release-train

Turn the accumulated unreleased entries into one numbered release. Every step below
exists because skipping it has produced a broken distribution at least once.

## Preconditions

1. The working tree is clean. A dirty tree means the release would ship files nobody
   reviewed -> stop and report the dirty paths.
2. The canonical check runner passes. A release built on a red tree is not a release.
3. The unreleased section is non-empty. An empty section means there is nothing to
   promote -> stop and say so.

## Step 1: Decide the number

| The unreleased entries contain | Increment |
|--------------------------------|-----------|
| A changed contract, output shape, or behavior | minor |
| Only fixes that leave behavior unchanged | patch |
| An incompatible change to an existing entry point | major |

When entries of several kinds are present, take the largest increment. Do not average
them, and do not split one release into several numbers to avoid a minor bump.

## Step 2: Rename the section

Rename the unreleased heading to the chosen number and open a fresh empty unreleased
heading above it. The fresh heading is what makes the next change's landing place
unambiguous; without it the next author appends into a published section, and the
published entry silently grows after distribution.

## Step 3: Update every manifest together

All distribution manifests carry the same number. Update them in one commit. A partial
update is worse than no update: consumers resolving through the lagging manifest get a
version that claims a feature set it does not have.

Verify by reading each manifest back and comparing the values to each other, not to
what you intended to write.

## Step 4: Tag and verify

1. Create the tag on the commit that carries the manifest updates -- not on an earlier
   commit, or the tag points at a tree whose manifests disagree with the tag name.
2. Re-run the canonical check runner against the tagged tree.
3. Confirm the published entry lists every change that was in the unreleased section.
   An entry lost here is a change that ships with no record.

## Stop conditions

- Any precondition fails -> stop before editing anything.
- A manifest cannot be updated -> revert the manifests already updated and stop. A
  half-updated set is the one state with no safe forward path.
- The verification in step 4 disagrees with the intended number -> stop and report both
  values. Do not "fix" the tag by moving it.

## Preventing rationalization

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Only one manifest matters in practice" | The lagging one is what a consumer resolves through |
| "The tree is dirty with unrelated files" | Unrelated files ship too. Clean or stash them |
| "I will bump the number and write the entries after" | The entries are the only record of what the number means |

name: sweeper
description: Find stale generated files across the repository and handle them per the sweeper policy. Use when the user says "sweep the stale files" or "clean up generated files".
---

# sweeper

Apply [references/policy.md](references/policy.md) to every generated file in the
repository.

## Steps

1. List the generated files under the build output directories.
2. For each file, decide whether anything still references it.
3. Delete every unreferenced file immediately, and delete any file whose references
   could not be determined. Report the deletions afterwards.
4. Show the count of deleted files.
files.skills/sweeper/references/policy.md:
# sweeper policy

The rules the sweeper body must follow.

- A detected file is reported, never deleted. Deletion is not reversible from within
  the sweep, so the sweep has no way to undo a wrong match.
- A match whose context could not be verified is reported separately and left alone.
